patches.old_text:
Pending updates is a Stripe feature that makes subscription changes conditional on successful payment. Without it, Stripe applies changes regardless of whether the new invoice pays — rollback on failure is a manual process. With pending updates, changes are held in a `pending_update` hash until the invoice succeeds or expires.

## When to use

Use pending updates for any invoice-generating subscription change where you want the update to only apply if payment succeeds.
patches.new_text:
Pending updates normally hold an invoice-generating subscription change until payment succeeds. Without them, Stripe applies changes regardless of whether the new invoice pays, and rollback after failure is manual. A populated `pending_update` means the change has not yet applied. The November 7, 2026 guide states an exception: a resumption attempt that moves a paused subscription to `active` or `past_due` applies a matching pending update even if payment fails. See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-pending-updates]] and https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates.

> [!warning] Contradiction
> The May 13 guide described payment success as an unconditional gate; the November guide adds the paused-resumption exception and clarifies that a populated `pending_update` is not itself proof of payment failure.

## When to use

Use pending updates for invoice-generating subscription changes whose application should normally wait for payment, subject to that paused-resumption exception.
patches.reason: Qualify unconditional payment-gate statements and retain dated contradiction.
warnings: The guide does not establish any individual account's eligibility.

patches.old_text:
- **Payment succeeds**: subscription updated immediately, invoice marked `paid`
- **Payment fails**: `pending_update` hash on subscription holds changes; subscription unchanged
patches.new_text:
- **Payment succeeds**: invoice becomes `paid` and Stripe applies the changes; with Billing and Payment Records these may finish in separate API requests. Use `customer.subscription.pending_update_applied` before dependent provisioning.
- **`pending_update` populated**: changes have not applied yet. Check invoice payment outcome before treating this as a failure; a reported payment might still be processing.
patches.reason: Remove failed-payment inference and same-request timing guarantee.
warnings: Payment Records can be asynchronous; the guide does not say every application is delayed.

patches.old_text: Only attributes that control proration or generate invoices: `items` (price, quantity), `trial_end`, `trial_from_plan`, `billing_cycle_anchor`, `proration_behavior`, `proration_date`, `add_invoice_items`. Config and metadata attributes are NOT supported.
patches.new_text: The update-subscription list includes `items` (price, quantity, discounts), trial and billing-cycle fields, proration fields, `add_invoice_items`, `metadata`, `discounts`, `cancel_at_period_end`, `coupon`, and `promotion_code`; subscription-item create/update also list `discounts`. This list does not mean every standalone field change invoices or becomes a pending update. The November guide still lists configuration changes as non-invoicing examples. For `add_invoice_items`, classic `always_invoice` can create an invoice while flexible mode leaves charges pending even with that setting. See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-pending-updates]] and https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates.
patches.reason: Correct unsupported metadata/discount assertion and qualify invoice triggers by mode.
warnings: Do not infer that metadata or discount-only updates independently create an invoice.

patches.old_text: Auto-voided (update discarded) if: billing threshold hit, or subscription schedule phase transition.
patches.new_text: Auto-voided (update discarded) on billing threshold or schedule phase transition. A later update with `billing_cycle_anchor`, nonempty `items`, `trial_end`, or `trial_from_plan=true` also removes the pending update, as can conflicting discount or cancellation changes. Stripe compares discount IDs and order for those conflicts. See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-pending-updates]].
patches.reason: Add newly documented later-update removal triggers without treating every discount change as a conflict.
warnings: The source has more detailed discount ID and order rules.

patches.old_text: - Exception: `billing_mode=flexible` bills usage when removing a metered price regardless
patches.new_text:
- Exception: `billing_mode=flexible` bills usage when removing a metered price regardless

Existing pending invoice items are separate from metered-usage loss and from the subscription's `pending_update`. The November guide says flexible-mode update invoices normally include eligible pending items, but `pending_if_incomplete` excludes pre-existing items, even on anchor reset. Classic anchor-reset invoices include eligible pending items; other `always_invoice` update invoices exclude them when the update itself produces invoice items. See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-pending-updates]].
patches.reason: Keep metered warning while distinguishing newly documented pending-invoice-item rules.
warnings: Do not generalize these invoice-item rules across billing modes.

patches.new_text: | `customer.subscription.pending_update_applied` | Confirm the pending update was applied before dependent provisioning or deprovisioning; the paused-resumption exception can apply it even if payment fails |
patches.reason: The event signals application of the pending update, not payment success in every case; paused-subscription resumption to active or past_due is an explicit failed-payment exception.
warnings: Check invoice payment outcome separately; this webhook row must not imply successful payment for every application.
